target: Setelah tiga bulan les, saya akhirnya bisa berenang sampai ujung kolam.
english: After three months of lessons, I can finally swim to the end of the pool.
grammar: Bisa = ability: bisa berenang = can swim. For permission Indonesian uses boleh, not bisa.

target: Adik saya belum bisa naik sepeda tanpa roda kecil di belakang.
english: My little brother can't ride a bike yet without the small wheels at the back.

target: Nenek masih bisa membaca koran pagi tanpa kacamata.
english: Grandma can still read the morning paper without glasses.

target: Kamu bisa mengangkat galon air itu sendirian?
english: Can you lift that water jug by yourself?

target: Dia bisa berbicara tiga bahasa karena keluarganya sering pindah negara.
english: He can speak three languages because his family often moved countries.

target: Saya tidak bisa membuka toples selai ini, tolong bukakan.
english: I can't open this jam jar; please open it for me.

target: Kalau jalan tol kosong, kita bisa sampai bandara dalam empat puluh menit.
english: If the toll road is empty, we can reach the airport in forty minutes.
grammar: Bisa also = possible: kita bisa sampai = we can (it is possible to) get there.

target: Motor tua ini masih bisa dipakai untuk keliling kampung.
english: This old motorbike can still be used for going around the neighborhood.

target: Setelah operasi lutut, kakek belum bisa berjalan jauh.
english: After his knee operation, Grandpa can't walk far yet.

target: Saya sudah bisa menyetir, tapi belum boleh membawa mobil sendirian.
english: I can already drive, but I'm not allowed to take the car out alone.
grammar: Bisa = able (skill), boleh = allowed (permission): bisa menyetir tapi belum boleh.

target: Anak itu sudah bisa berenang, tapi belum boleh masuk kolam yang dalam.
english: That child can swim already, but isn't allowed into the deep pool yet.

target: Kartu ini bisa dipakai di bus, tapi tidak bisa dipakai di kereta bandara.
english: This card can be used on the bus, but can't be used on the airport train.

target: Boleh saya pinjam tangga kamu untuk mengganti lampu teras?
english: May I borrow your ladder to change the porch light?
grammar: Boleh saya...? = May I...? — the everyday way to ask permission: Boleh saya pinjam...?

target: Boleh saya pinjam gunting sebentar? Punya saya hilang entah ke mana.
english: May I borrow your scissors for a moment? Mine disappeared who knows where.

target: Bukunya boleh dipinjam dua minggu dan bisa diperpanjang satu kali.
english: The book may be borrowed for two weeks and can be extended once.
grammar: Rules pair them: boleh dipinjam = allowed to be borrowed, bisa diperpanjang = possible to extend.

target: Pak, boleh saya memakai ruang rapat kecil untuk menelepon klien?
english: Sir, may I use the small meeting room to call a client?

target: Bu, boleh saya minta izin datang siang besok karena ada urusan keluarga?
english: Ma'am, may I have permission to come in late tomorrow because of a family matter?
grammar: Minta izin = ask permission: minta izin datang siang = ask to come in late.

target: Boleh anak-anak berenang di kolam dangkal tanpa pelampung?
english: May the children swim in the shallow pool without floaties?

target: Maaf, pengunjung tidak boleh membawa makanan dari luar ke area kolam.
english: Sorry, visitors may not bring outside food into the pool area.

target: Kamu boleh memakai mobil ayah, asal pulang sebelum jam sepuluh malam.
english: You may use Dad's car, as long as you come home before ten at night.
grammar: Asal = as long as: boleh, asal pulang sebelum malam = allowed, provided you're home early.

target: Boleh saya menyalakan kipas angin? Ruangan ini panas sekali.
english: May I turn on the fan? This room is really hot.

target: Tamu hotel boleh memakai kolam renang sampai jam sembilan malam.
english: Hotel guests may use the swimming pool until nine at night.

target: Maaf Pak, di sini tidak boleh merokok, area merokok ada di lantai satu.
english: Sorry sir, smoking isn't allowed here; the smoking area is on the first floor.
grammar: Tidak boleh = not allowed (spoken): tidak boleh merokok. Signs say dilarang merokok.

target: Karyawan tidak boleh menerima hadiah mahal dari klien perusahaan.
english: Employees may not accept expensive gifts from company clients.

target: Di perpustakaan kampus, pengunjung tidak boleh berbicara keras-keras.
english: In the campus library, visitors may not talk loudly.

target: Boleh saya membawa anjing kecil saya masuk ke kafe ini?
english: May I bring my small dog into this cafe?

target: Anak-anak boleh bermain di halaman sampai lampu jalan menyala.
english: The children may play in the yard until the streetlights come on.

target: Boleh saya menitip tas di sini selama saya berenang?
english: May I leave my bag here while I swim?

target: Boleh saya mengganti jadwal les piano anak saya minggu ini?
english: May I change my child's piano lesson schedule this week?

target: Kata dokter, ayah sudah boleh pulang dari rumah sakit besok pagi.
english: The doctor says Dad is allowed to go home from the hospital tomorrow morning.
grammar: Sudah boleh = allowed now (was not before): sudah boleh pulang = can finally go home.

target: Setelah dua minggu, jahitannya sudah kering dan saya boleh berenang lagi.
english: After two weeks, the stitches were dry and I was allowed to swim again.

target: Boleh saya duduk di sini, atau kursi ini sudah ada yang punya?
english: May I sit here, or is this seat taken?

target: Semua tamu harus menulis nama di buku tamu sebelum masuk gedung.
english: All guests must write their name in the guest book before entering the building.

target: Saya harus menjemput anak saya sebelum kelas renangnya selesai jam lima.
english: I have to pick up my child before her swimming class ends at five.

target: Di rumah kami, sepatu harus dilepas sebelum naik ke lantai kayu.
english: In our house, shoes must be taken off before stepping onto the wooden floor.
grammar: House rules use harus + di-: sepatu harus dilepas = shoes must be taken off.

target: Kamu harus mengembalikan raket ini ke loket sebelum gedung olahraga tutup.
english: You have to return this racket to the counter before the sports hall closes.

target: Sebelum wawancara kerja, kamu harus menyiapkan cerita tentang pengalamanmu.
english: Before a job interview, you have to prepare stories about your experience.

target: Obat batuk ini harus dihabiskan walaupun kamu sudah merasa sehat.
english: This cough medicine must be finished even if you already feel healthy.

target: Kami harus mengganti ban belakang sebelum berangkat ke luar kota.
english: We have to change the rear tire before leaving town.

target: Kamu tidak harus ikut arisan, tapi ibu pasti senang kalau kamu datang.
english: You don't have to join the arisan, but Mom will definitely be happy if you come.
grammar: Tidak harus = don't have to (optional) — NOT forbidden. 'Must not' is tidak boleh.

target: Laporan bulanan harus dikirim ke pusat paling lambat tanggal lima.
english: The monthly report must be sent to head office by the fifth at the latest.
grammar: Paling lambat = at the latest: paling lambat tanggal lima = by the fifth at the latest.

target: Sebelum kelas yoga dimulai, semua peserta harus mengisi formulir kesehatan.
english: Before the yoga class starts, all participants must fill in a health form.

target: Pengemudi harus membawa SIM dan STNK setiap kali berkendara.
english: Drivers must carry their license and vehicle papers whenever they drive.

target: Saya harus menabung enam bulan lagi supaya uang mukanya cukup.
english: I have to save for six more months so the down payment is enough.

target: Kalau mau ikut lomba renang antarkantor, kamu harus mendaftar minggu ini.
english: If you want to join the inter-office swimming competition, you have to register this week.

target: Anak kucing itu harus diberi susu tiga jam sekali.
english: That kitten has to be given milk every three hours.

target: Kenapa formulir ini harus dicetak, tidak bisa dikirim lewat email saja?
english: Why does this form have to be printed — can't it just be sent by email?
grammar: Harus = must, bisa = can: harus dicetak, tidak bisa lewat email = must be printed, can't go by email.

target: Sebelum pindah, kami harus memberi tahu pemilik kos satu bulan sebelumnya.
english: Before moving out, we have to inform the boarding-house owner one month in advance.

target: Sebaiknya kamu berangkat sebelum jam tujuh supaya tidak kena macet.
english: You'd better leave before seven so you don't get stuck in traffic.
grammar: Sebaiknya = you'd better / it's best to — advice, much softer than harus.

target: Kalau demamnya belum turun besok, sebaiknya kamu periksa ke dokter.
english: If the fever hasn't gone down by tomorrow, you'd better see a doctor.

target: Sebaiknya kita membawa jas hujan, langit di barat mulai gelap.
english: We'd better bring raincoats; the sky in the west is getting dark.

target: Waktu bepergian, sebaiknya uang tunai disimpan di dua tempat berbeda.
english: When traveling, it's best to keep cash in two different places.

target: Sebaiknya jangan menaruh dompet di saku belakang waktu naik bus kota.
english: Better not to put your wallet in your back pocket when riding the city bus.
grammar: Sebaiknya jangan = better not to — a gentle warning, friendlier than a flat jangan.

target: Menurut pelatih, sebaiknya kami pemanasan sepuluh menit sebelum angkat beban.
english: According to the coach, we should warm up for ten minutes before lifting weights.

target: Sebaiknya daging ini dimasak hari ini juga supaya tidak bau.
english: This meat had better be cooked today so it doesn't smell.

target: Kamu sebaiknya minta maaf dulu, urusan siapa yang salah bisa nanti.
english: You'd better apologize first; whose fault it is can wait.
grammar: Sebaiknya can follow the subject: kamu sebaiknya minta maaf = you'd better apologize.

target: Sebaiknya kita pesan taksi dari sekarang, malam ini banyak acara di kota.
english: We'd better book a taxi now; there are lots of events in town tonight.

target: Untuk pemula, sebaiknya mulai dari beban yang paling ringan dulu.
english: For beginners, it's best to start with the lightest weights first.

target: Kamu mesti coba sate ayam di warung dekat stasiun itu.
english: You've got to try the chicken satay at the stall near the station.
grammar: Mesti = harus in relaxed speech — you'll hear it everywhere. In writing and formal talk, use harus.

target: Kalau ke Yogyakarta, kamu mesti mampir ke pasar malamnya.
english: If you go to Yogyakarta, you've got to stop by its night market.

target: Saya mesti pulang sekarang, besok ujian saya mulai pagi-pagi.
english: I've got to go home now; my exam starts early tomorrow.

target: Kita mesti berangkat lebih pagi kalau tidak mau antre lama di loket.
english: We've got to leave earlier if we don't want to queue long at the ticket window.

target: Lemari seberat itu mesti diangkat dua orang, jangan coba angkat sendirian.
english: A wardrobe that heavy has to be lifted by two people — don't try lifting it alone.

target: Mesti sabar ya, hasil tes darahnya baru keluar hari Kamis.
english: You've just got to be patient; the blood test results only come out on Thursday.

target: Ban depannya sudah tipis, mesti diganti sebelum musim hujan.
english: The front tire is already worn thin; it's got to be replaced before the rainy season.

target: Kamu mesti tanya harga dulu sebelum naik ojek di tempat wisata.
english: You've got to ask the price first before taking a motorbike taxi at tourist spots.

target: Mesti ada orang dewasa di rumah kalau tukang gas datang.
english: There has to be an adult at home when the gas man comes.

target: Di undangan tertulis jam tujuh, berarti kita mesti keluar rumah jam enam.
english: The invitation says seven, which means we've got to leave the house at six.
grammar: Berarti = that means: berarti kita mesti keluar jam enam = so we've got to leave at six.

target: Sebelum naik pesawat, kami masih sempat membeli oleh-oleh di bandara.
english: Before boarding the plane, we still managed to buy souvenirs at the airport.
grammar: Sempat = managed to / had time to: masih sempat membeli = still managed to buy.

target: Tadi pagi saya tidak sempat sarapan karena bangun kesiangan.
english: This morning I didn't have time for breakfast because I woke up too late.
grammar: Tidak sempat = didn't get the chance: tidak sempat sarapan = no time for breakfast.

target: Untung kami sempat berteduh di halte sebelum hujannya tambah deras.
english: Luckily we managed to take shelter at the bus stop before the rain got heavier.

target: Dia sempat bekerja dua tahun di Makassar sebelum pindah ke Jakarta.
english: He worked for two years in Makassar at one point before moving to Jakarta.
grammar: Sempat + job/place = once did for a while: sempat bekerja di Makassar = worked there at one point.

target: Kamu sempat bertemu Bu Sari kemarin sebelum beliau pindah ke cabang baru?
english: Did you get a chance to meet Mrs. Sari yesterday before she moved to the new branch?

target: Maaf, saya belum sempat membalas pesanmu, minggu ini penuh sekali.
english: Sorry, I haven't had a chance to reply to your message; this week is completely full.

target: Kemarin sore kami sempat mampir sebentar ke rumah nenek.
english: Yesterday afternoon we managed to stop by Grandma's house for a bit.

target: Sebelum listriknya mati, saya sempat menyimpan semua pekerjaan di laptop.
english: Before the power went out, I managed to save all my work on the laptop.

target: Dia tidak sempat makan siang karena rapatnya mundur ke jam satu.
english: He didn't get a chance to eat lunch because the meeting was pushed back to one.

target: Kami hanya sempat melihat candi utama karena sorenya hujan deras.
english: We only had time to see the main temple because it rained hard in the afternoon.

target: Saya sempat bingung di stasiun karena nama jalurnya mirip semua.
english: I was confused for a moment at the station because the platform names all look alike.
grammar: Sempat + feeling = briefly felt: sempat bingung = was confused for a moment.

target: Untung kamu datang, saya sempat berpikir acaranya batal.
english: Good thing you came — for a moment I thought the event was canceled.

target: Saya tidak sanggup menghabiskan porsi nasi padang sebesar ini.
english: I can't manage to finish a Padang rice portion this big.
grammar: Sanggup = can manage/handle it — heavier than bisa: tidak sanggup menghabiskan = can't finish it.

target: Kamu sanggup menyelesaikan revisi laporan ini sebelum Jumat sore?
english: Can you manage to finish the report revisions before Friday afternoon?

target: Setelah latihan setahun, dia sanggup berlari sepuluh kilometer tanpa berhenti.
english: After a year of training, he can run ten kilometers without stopping.

target: Kami tidak sanggup membayar sewa apartemen di tengah kota lagi.
english: We can't afford the rent on an apartment downtown anymore.
grammar: Tidak sanggup + a cost = can't afford: tidak sanggup membayar sewa = can't afford the rent.

target: Kalau tidak sanggup lembur malam ini, bilang ke Pak Anton sekarang.
english: If you can't manage overtime tonight, tell Mr. Anton now.

target: Dia sanggup menunggu dua jam demi tiket konser band favoritnya.
english: He was willing to wait two hours for tickets to his favorite band's concert.
grammar: Demi = for the sake of: demi tiket konser = for the sake of concert tickets.

target: Ibu tidak sanggup melihat film sedih, pasti langsung menangis.
english: Mom can't handle sad movies; she always cries right away.

target: Satu ember penuh begini, kamu sanggup membawanya naik ke lantai tiga?
english: A bucket this full — can you manage to carry it up to the third floor?
grammar: -nya can be 'it' after a verb: membawanya = carry it.

target: Mereka sanggup membuka warung lagi enam bulan setelah kebakaran itu.
english: They managed to open their food stall again six months after the fire.

target: Setelah cedera bahu, berapa kilo yang sanggup kamu angkat sekarang?
english: After your shoulder injury, how many kilos can you manage to lift now?

target: Tidak usah membawa apa-apa besok, cukup datang saja lebih awal.
english: No need to bring anything tomorrow; just come a bit early.
grammar: Tidak usah = no need to (relaxed). Jangan = don't! (warning) — tidak usah bayar is not jangan bayar.

target: Kamu tidak usah menjemput saya, dari stasiun saya naik ojek saja.
english: You don't need to pick me up; I'll just take a motorbike taxi from the station.

target: Tidak usah repot-repot masak, kami benar-benar hanya mampir sebentar.
english: Please don't go to the trouble of cooking; we're really only stopping by for a moment.
grammar: Tidak usah repot-repot = don't go to any trouble — the polite guest's phrase.

target: Piringnya tidak usah dicuci sekarang, biar saya yang beres-beres nanti.
english: No need to wash the dishes now; let me tidy up later.
grammar: Biar saya yang... = let me be the one to: biar saya yang beres-beres = let me tidy up.

target: Kalau lukanya sekecil itu, tidak usah ke rumah sakit.
english: If the wound is that small, there's no need to go to the hospital.

target: Tidak usah malu bertanya, pelatih di sini semuanya ramah.
english: No need to be shy about asking; the trainers here are all friendly.

target: Bilang ke ibu tidak usah masak malam ini, kita makan di luar.
english: Tell Mom she doesn't need to cook tonight; we're eating out.

target: Tiketnya sudah saya beli lewat aplikasi, kamu tidak usah antre.
english: I already bought the tickets through the app; you don't need to queue.

target: Tidak usah menunggu saya untuk makan malam, rapatnya selesai larut malam.
english: No need to wait for me for dinner; the meeting ends late at night.

target: Kata teknisinya, mesin cucinya tidak usah diganti, cukup diperbaiki saja.
english: The technician says the washing machine doesn't need replacing; it just needs repairing.
grammar: Tidak usah works in passives too: tidak usah diganti = doesn't need to be replaced.

target: Tidak usah dibungkus, saya makan di sini saja.
english: No need to wrap it up; I'll just eat here.

target: Untuk kelas percobaan, tidak usah bayar, cukup isi formulir pendaftaran.
english: For the trial class, no need to pay; just fill in the registration form.

target: Silakan menaruh sepatu di rak dekat pintu sebelum masuk.
english: Please put your shoes on the rack by the door before coming in.
grammar: Silakan = please, go ahead. In Java you'll often hear monggo — same warm invitation.

target: Silakan mengambil teh hangat di meja sambil menunggu giliran Anda.
english: Please help yourself to warm tea at the table while waiting for your turn.

target: Kalau mau tambah nasi, silakan ambil sendiri di dapur.
english: If you want more rice, please help yourself in the kitchen.

target: Silakan duduk dulu, dokter giginya masih memeriksa pasien lain.
english: Please have a seat; the dentist is still examining another patient.

target: Silakan memakai loker mana saja yang masih kosong.
english: Please use any locker that's still empty.
grammar: Mana saja = any/whichever: loker mana saja = any locker at all.

target: Silakan hubungi resepsionis kalau AC kamarnya kurang dingin.
english: Please contact reception if the room's air conditioning isn't cold enough.

target: Silakan masuk lewat pintu samping, pintu depannya sedang dicat ulang.
english: Please come in through the side door; the front door is being repainted.

target: Silakan dicicipi dulu sambalnya, jangan takut, tidak terlalu pedas.
english: Please have a taste of the sambal first; don't be afraid, it's not too spicy.
grammar: Silakan di- + verb = extra polite invitation: silakan dicicipi = please do have a taste.

target: Pengunjung kolam wajib mandi di pancuran sebelum masuk ke air.
english: Pool visitors are required to shower before entering the water.
grammar: Wajib = required — the word of rules and signs. In conversation people say harus.

target: Anggota baru wajib mengikuti kelas pengenalan alat sebelum latihan sendiri.
english: New members are required to take an equipment orientation class before training alone.

target: Semua tamu gedung wajib menukar kartu identitas dengan kartu pengunjung.
english: All building guests are required to exchange their ID card for a visitor card.

target: Penumpang wajib memakai sabuk pengaman selama pesawat lepas landas dan mendarat.
english: Passengers are required to wear seatbelts while the plane takes off and lands.
grammar: Announcements use formal wajib: penumpang wajib memakai = passengers are required to wear.

target: Peserta lomba lari wajib mengambil nomor dada sehari sebelum acara.
english: Race participants are required to collect their bib numbers the day before the event.

target: Pengendara motor wajib memakai helm walaupun jaraknya hanya lima menit.
english: Motorbike riders are required to wear a helmet even if the trip is only five minutes.

target: Anggota wajib mengembalikan barbel ke raknya setelah selesai dipakai.
english: Members are required to return the dumbbells to the rack after use.

target: Anak di bawah sepuluh tahun wajib ditemani orang dewasa di kolam ini.
english: Children under ten must be accompanied by an adult in this pool.

target: Di area kolam dilarang berlari, lantainya licin sekali kalau basah.
english: Running is forbidden in the pool area; the floor is very slippery when wet.
grammar: Dilarang = forbidden (sign language): dilarang berlari = no running. Spoken: jangan lari.

target: Dilarang membawa tas besar ke dalam ruang latihan, silakan pakai loker.
english: Large bags are not allowed in the training room; please use a locker.

target: Di ruang ganti ini dilarang memotret, demi kenyamanan semua anggota.
english: Photography is forbidden in this changing room, for the comfort of all members.
grammar: Memotret = to photograph (from potret): dilarang memotret = no photography.

target: Sampah wajib dibuang di tempat yang sudah disediakan.
english: Trash must be thrown in the bins provided.

target: Peminjam wajib melapor kalau alat olahraga rusak waktu dipakai.
english: Borrowers are required to report it if sports equipment breaks during use.

target: Petugas wajib memeriksa kebersihan air kolam setiap pagi sebelum jam buka.
english: Staff are required to check the cleanliness of the pool water every morning before opening time.

target: Di papan itu tertulis wajib, jadi ini aturan, bukan sekadar saran.
english: The sign says 'wajib', so this is a rule, not just a suggestion.
grammar: Wajib = a rule that binds; saran = a suggestion. Signs with wajib are not optional.
